source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed brake tests in a vehicle inspection report

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
2. Note the date and time of inspection, as well as the identification details of the vehicle, such as make, model, VIN, registration, and license plate number. Include the odometer reading and the name of the inspecting technician.

3. Conduct the brake test using an approved method, such as a roller brake tester, a decelerometer, or a track test, depending upon the inspection standards and equipment available.

4. Record the results of the brake test, providing numerical measurements where applicable, such as deceleration rates, pedal effort, and brake balance percentages.

5. List any observed abnormalities during the test, such as pulsation, noise, drag, or uneven brake engagement. Note any visual observations of the brake system, like leaking fluids, worn pads, or damaged rotors.

6. Check all components of the brake system, including the pedal free play, master cylinder, brake lines, hoses, calipers, drums, rot
